it’s pretty remarkable that meta is effectively bundling a growing number of ai utilities into its products & giving them away for ~free.

this is how social media became completely free. you can imagine the same thing happening across ai. entire categories that currently support billion dollar companies could get bundled into muse.

meta is structurally incentivized to do this cuz the product doesn’t need to monetize directly if it increases engagement, retention, or the value of the network + creates entirely new business opportunities like agentic commerce.

in some sense, zuck is commodifying the product layer of ai way more than the model layer. that’s pretty hefty competition for a lot of product companies.

i suspect muse for business (not just consumers) will be built at some point too.

candidates.text:
Things mental contraction / clenching is bad for:

- Doing cognitive tasks
- Connecting deeply with friends
- Having fun
- Attracting a partner
- Making love
- Living more consciously 
- Gaining insight into reality 
- Reducing baseline suffering 

Things clenching / mental contraction can sometimes be for:

- Running away from predators 
- Hunting prey
- Navigating emergency life or death situations 
- Protecting your psyche from sensory overload / traumas it’s not ready to process 

Most of us don’t spend much time hunting prey, running away from predators or navigating emergency life or death situations.

And most of us spend a lot of time engaged in social / romantic / cognitive / (and for some) meditative activities.

So, really the only limiting factor on the speed and frequency at which it makes sense to unclench / decontract / open awareness is the degree to which we have traumas we are not ready to process / sensory environments that overwhelm us.

This simultaneously points to how healing trauma is deeply intertwined with the journey of opening awareness, and also shows how other than that consideration we have absolutely nothing to fear about unclenching / de contracting / opening awareness.

We just need to give our fearful parts enough exposure to more open states of awareness to help them overcome their fear of them.

The Review Exercise QTd below can also accelerate this process.

candidates.text:
If 80% of your email flow revenue is coming from your welcome series, your retention is in serious trouble

Most founders look at that number and celebrate

What it actually means:

- You are dependent on expensive front-end ad spend
- Once someone buys, your post-purchase engine goes completely dark
- You have zero automated systems driving repeat purchases, cross-sells, or churn reduction

A healthy email engine should generate 60%+ of its automated revenue *after* the first purchase:

Day 1 to 14: Consumption and routine onboarding (kill buyer remorse)
Day 15 to 30: Second purchase bridge or subscription upgrade
Day 30 to 60: Category cross-sells based on what they actually ordered
Day 60+: Smart replenishment triggers timed to product depletion

If your welcome series is carrying your entire email channel, you aren't running retention marketing

You're just running an expensive coupon delivery service for new traffic
